Entries 13, 14 and 16 ("**Manager** na access role para sa serbisyo", "**Administrator**/**Viewer** na access role para sa pamamahala ng platform") correctly separate service access from platform access. The one issue is consistency. Entries 30 and 31 now use Tagalog ("Lahat ng serbisyo ng IAM Account Management", "Serbisyo ng Support Center"), but the policy labels right next to them in entries 28 and 29 stay in English ("All Account Management services (viewer)"). Translating only this item makes the list inconsistent, and the name no longer matches the console label the reader has to find.

That breaks the pattern of the sibling heading in entry 16 ("Mga AI circuit synthesis pass"). It also no longer matches entry 36, which links to this section as "[AI routing pass]", so a learner following that link lands on a heading worded differently. examples.source: AI routing pass {#ai-routing-pass}
examples.translation: Pass ng AI routing {#ai-routing-pass}
examples.suggested: AI routing pass {#ai-routing-pass}

editor_note: The five short entries are faithful and read naturally in casual Taglish, for example "Na-release ang skill na `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime` ... para sa pag-migrate ng code" and "Changelog ng Qiskit skills", and none of them drift from the English meaning.

Faithful overall. Dates, quantities, retirement caveats and the Qiskit Runtime rename architecture ([41]-[51]) all carry over correctly. A few sentences are garbled or slightly shifted, but none would mislead a learner. [199] uses "nakikinabang sa mga user" ("benefits from users"), which flips the roles; the next sentence is correct, so context recovers it. [220] turns a simple bug fix into a confusing double negative ("nagpapabalewala sa QPU metrics na hindi maipakita"). [280] renders "circuits of interest" as "circuit na kagustuhan" and has the typo "maaari ng" (should be "maaari nang"). [236] "na na-access mo" says "systems you have accessed" instead of "systems you have access to". [203] is ungrammatical ("hindi mo na magiging accessible"). There are also light formal slips such as "mangyaring" and "Kami ay excited".

examples.source: This update benefits users who manage multiple instances
examples.translation: Ang update na ito ay nakikinabang sa mga user na namamahala ng maraming instance
examples.suggested: Makikinabang sa update na ito ang mga user na namamahala ng maraming instance
examples.why: 'nakikinabang sa' means 'benefits from', so the sentence says the update benefits from the users. That reverses who benefits.

examples.source: Addressed an issue that prevented QPU metrics to be displayed for the QPUs in the eu-de region.
examples.translation: Naayos ang isyung nagpapabalewala sa QPU metrics na hindi maipakita para sa mga QPU sa eu-de region.
examples.suggested: Naayos ang isyung pumipigil sa pagpapakita ng QPU metrics para sa mga QPU sa eu-de region.
examples.why: 'nagpapabalewala' (nullifies) combined with 'hindi maipakita' makes a confusing double negative. The bug fix itself is simple.

examples.source: affecting the gates in one or more circuits of interest ... can then be passed to Estimator
examples.translation: sa isa o higit pang mga circuit na kagustuhan ... ay maaari ng ipasa sa Estimator
examples.suggested: sa isa o higit pang circuit na pinag-aaralan ... ay maaari nang ipasa sa Estimator
examples.why: 'kagustuhan' means preference or desire, not 'of interest'. 'maaari ng' is a typo for 'maaari nang'.

examples.source: View the systems you have access to with your selected instance
examples.translation: Tingnan ang mga system na na-access mo gamit ang iyong napiling instance
examples.suggested: Tingnan ang mga system na may access ka gamit ang iyong napiling instance
examples.why: 'na-access mo' means systems you have already accessed, not systems you are entitled to use.

examples.source: you will no longer have access to this platform or its data
examples.translation: hindi mo na magiging accessible ang platform na ito o ang datos nito
examples.suggested: wala ka nang access sa platform na ito o sa datos nito
examples.why: Ungrammatical calque of 'have access'. A native editor would rewrite it.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten headings changes the meaning, but they don't match the rest of the page. The sibling heading [16] stays "`if` statement", and the construct list ([11]-[13]) and the body text ([27], [29], [33], [37]) use "switch statement", "for loop" and "while loop". Only these three headings use "Pahayag na switch", "Loop na For" and "Loop na While". The capitalized "For"/"While" in the Tagalog word order also reads like a stiff calque of keywords that should be lowercase, so a native editor would change the headings to match the kept-English terms used everywhere else on the page.

examples.source: Switch statement {#switch-statement}
examples.translation: Pahayag na switch {#switch-statement}
examples.suggested: Switch statement {#switch-statement}
examples.why: The sibling heading [16] keeps "`if` statement", and [11]/[27]/[29] all say "switch statement". Only this heading translates it as "Pahayag", so the term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: For loop {#for-loop}
examples.translation: Loop na For {#for-loop}
examples.suggested: For loop {#for-loop}
examples.why: The capitalized keyword "For" in this Tagalog word order is a stiff calque. The list [12] and the body [33] use "for loop", so the heading doesn't match the text under it.

examples.source: While loop {#while-loop}
examples.translation: Loop na While {#while-loop}
examples.suggested: While loop {#while-loop}
examples.why: Same problem as the For loop heading: the list [13] and the body [37] use "while loop", so "Loop na While" breaks consistency and capitalizes a lowercase keyword.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English: entry 14 keeps the bolded negation ("**hindi** nakakabit sa isang umiiral na IBM Cloud account"), and entry 41 renders all five topic links correctly ("Bawasan ang job run time", "I-monitor o i-cancel ang isang job").

Entry 11 ("Open-source ba ang Quantum Compute?") is faithful and reads naturally. Entry 23 turns the product name "Qiskit Functions" into a plural common noun, "Mga Qiskit Function". The rest of the page keeps the name as it is: entry 0 has "Qiskit Functions", entry 24 has "Ang Qiskit Functions" and entry 27 has "dokumentasyon ng Qiskit Functions". The heading should keep the proper name. A learner would not be misled, but this is an inconsistency a native editor would fix.

examples.source: Qiskit Functions {#qiskit-functions}
examples.translation: Mga Qiskit Function {#qiskit-functions}
examples.suggested: Qiskit Functions {#qiskit-functions}
examples.why: 'Qiskit Functions' is the name of an IBM service. Treating it as a plural common noun ('Mga ... Function') breaks up the name and clashes with entries 0, 24 and 27, which keep 'Qiskit Functions' unchanged.

editor_note: Entry 27 keeps the meaning. It gives the 250 microseconds default, says lowering `rep_delay` cuts total QPU execution time, and keeps the higher state-preparation error rate. The one problem is "sa gastos ng", a word-for-word copy of the English idiom "at the expense of". It reads stiffly, and on a page about usage and billing "gastos" can make a reader think of money. A native editor would write "kapalit ng" instead.

examples.source: decreases the total QPU execution time, but at the expense of increased state preparation error rate
examples.translation: nagpapababa ng kabuuang oras ng pagpapatupad ng QPU, ngunit sa gastos ng mas mataas na error rate sa state preparation
examples.suggested: nagpapababa ng kabuuang oras ng pagpapatupad ng QPU, ngunit kapalit nito ang mas mataas na error rate sa state preparation
examples.why: 'sa gastos ng' copies the English idiom word for word and isn't natural Tagalog. On a billing page, 'gastos' can also suggest money. 'kapalit nito' states the trade-off in natural Tagalog.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [8] keeps the full disclaimer ("hindi sumasalamin sa opisyal na patakaran o posisyon ng IBM o ng IBM Quantum team"), and [12] renders "Sa papel na ito, ginamit namin ang `ibmq_vigo`, na isa sa mga IBM Quantum Canary processor" with nothing dropped or added.

None of the four rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 27) would mislead a learner, and entries 4 and 27 are faithful and natural. The problems are in the admonition. In entry 6, "ay karamihan drop-in replacement" is ungrammatical. It could also be read as "most of these primitives are drop-in replacements", when the English means each one is "largely" a drop-in replacement. In entry 5, "finer control" became "mas mahusay na kontrol" ("better control"), which loses the idea of more detailed control, and "inililipat ang execution" is a slightly odd way to say "delegate".

examples.source: these client-side primitives are largely drop-in replacements of the legacy server-side primitives
examples.translation: ang mga client-side na primitive na ito ay karamihan drop-in replacement ng mga legacy server-side na primitive
examples.suggested: ang mga client-side na primitive na ito ay halos drop-in replacement ng mga legacy server-side na primitive
examples.why: 'karamihan' means 'most of' and doesn't work as an adverb here. It reads as ungrammatical and could be taken as 'most of these primitives'. 'halos' (or 'sa malaking bahagi') gives the English meaning of 'largely'.

examples.source: faster debugging feedback, and finer control
examples.translation: mas mabilis na debugging feedback, at mas mahusay na kontrol
examples.suggested: mas mabilis na debugging feedback, at mas detalyadong kontrol
examples.why: 'finer' means more granular or detailed control, but 'mas mahusay' only says 'better'. It's a slight softening of the claim, not misleading.

examples.source: delegate execution to the Executor primitive
examples.translation: inililipat ang execution sa Executor primitive
examples.suggested: ipinapasa ang execution sa Executor primitive
examples.why: 'ipinapasa' ('passes on') is closer to 'delegate' than 'inililipat' ('moves/transfers') and is more natural for handing off a task.

editor_note: Entry 60 keeps the meaning: "mas tumpak na mga resulta, ngunit nangangailangan ng mas mahabang oras ng pagproseso" correctly carries the accuracy-versus-time trade-off, and nothing was added or dropped. The one problem is word order copied from English. In "teknik para mabawasan ang mga error na tinatawag na [dynamical decoupling]", the linker "na" attaches to the nearest noun, "mga error", so the Tagalog reads as though the errors are called dynamical decoupling instead of the technique. The link and the word "teknik" make the intended meaning recoverable, so this is a minor fix, not a fail. Moving the name next to "teknik" fixes it.

examples.source: by using a technique to reduce errors called [dynamical decoupling]
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng teknik para mabawasan ang mga error na tinatawag na [dynamical decoupling]
examples.suggested: gamit ang teknik na tinatawag na [dynamical decoupling], na nagbabawas ng mga error
examples.why: Word order copied from English: in Tagalog, 'na tinatawag na' attaches to 'mga error', so the sentence says the errors, not the technique, are called dynamical decoupling.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout, and core terms stay consistent (ansatz, transpile/tine-transpile, backend, shots, ground state). There are a few wording slips. In [21], "binababa ng hardware noise ang resulta" says noise "lowers" the result. On an energy-minimization page, a lower result sounds like a better one. In [32], "far better results" became "mas malaki ang naibibigay na resulta", which drops the "far". In [26], "reports" is rendered "Inilathala" ("published"), and [16] has the calque "ay pagkatapos post-processed".

examples.source: hardware noise degrades the optimizer result where it reverts to raw values matching random sampling
examples.translation: binababa ng hardware noise ang resulta ng optimizer kung saan ito bumabalik sa raw values na katumbas ng random sampling
examples.suggested: pinapababa ng hardware noise ang kalidad ng resulta ng optimizer, kaya bumabalik ito sa raw values na katumbas ng random sampling
examples.why: 'binababa ang resulta' literally means 'lowers the result'. Where lower energy is better, that could read as an improvement. The next clause does make the meaning clear, though.

examples.source: for larger instances, the optimizer gives far better results
examples.translation: para sa mas malalaking instance, mas malaki ang naibibigay na resulta ng optimizer
examples.suggested: para sa mas malalaking instance, mas mahusay nang malaki ang resulta ng optimizer
examples.why: The translation drops the intensifier 'far' and changes 'better' to 'larger'. That is defensible for an MIS size, but the claim comes out softer.

examples.source: Table 1 reports averaged values ... The minimum MS violation ... is reported.
examples.translation: Inilathala ng Table 1 ang averaged values ... Inilathala ang minimum MS violation
examples.suggested: Ipinapakita ng Table 1 ang averaged values ... Iniuulat ang minimum MS violation
examples.why: 'Inilathala' means 'published'. It is the wrong verb for a table reporting values.

examples.source: Raw results are then post-processed.
examples.translation: Ang raw results ay pagkatapos post-processed.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, dumadaan sa post-processing ang raw results.
examples.why: This is a calque of the English passive, with an unconjugated English participle and an adverb in the wrong place.

editor_note: Entry 24 is the only entry reviewed here. Its heading was rewritten as "Mapa ng coupling". The meaning is still correct, but the body of the section never uses that phrase. It keeps the English term "coupling map" throughout: entries 0, 23, 25 ("Ang coupling map ay isang graph..."), 26 and 28 (which passes the `coupling_map` argument). Nobody would be misled, but the heading no longer matches the term the section teaches, so a learner might not connect the two. Using "Coupling map" in the heading would keep the file consistent.

examples.source: Coupling map {#coupling-map}
examples.translation: Mapa ng coupling {#coupling-map}
examples.suggested: Coupling map {#coupling-map}
examples.why: The body of the section keeps the English term 'coupling map' every time (entries 23, 25, 26, 28), so this translated heading is inconsistent with the file. It also reads like a half-calque. The meaning is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: Entry 6 keeps the English meaning. The caveat is intact ("hindi palaging katulad" for "do not necessarily reflect"), and it still says the reference primitives do not support noise modeling while Aer's do. The one thing to fix is "isang mataas na performansyang quantum circuit simulator". "Performansyang" is an awkward coinage, and the same sentence then translates "performance" differently as "pagganap" ("mas magandang pagganap"), so one English word gets two renderings a few words apart. Using one term for both, or keeping "high-performance", would read more naturally.

examples.line_approx: Ang Qiskit Aer ay isang mataas na performansyang quantum circuit simulator...
examples.source: Qiskit Aer is a high-performance quantum circuit simulator that you can use in place of the reference primitives for better performance and more features.
examples.translation: Ang Qiskit Aer ay isang mataas na performansyang quantum circuit simulator na maaari mong gamitin bilang kapalit ng mga reference primitive para sa mas magandang pagganap at mas maraming tampok.
examples.suggested: Ang Qiskit Aer ay isang high-performance na quantum circuit simulator na maaari mong gamitin kapalit ng mga reference primitive para sa mas mabilis na pagganap at mas maraming tampok.
examples.why: 'Mataas na performansyang' is a stiff coinage, and 'performance' is translated two different ways in the same sentence (performansya / pagganap).

editor_note: Rewritten entry 17 heading "Superdense Coding" keeps the protocol name in English, matching the body's "superdense coding" in entries 18-21, and does not change the meaning (the title-case capitalization is left to the separate kept-term sweep).

All three rewritten entries are faithful and natural, including the Credly notice [12], which keeps the "Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM" hedge for "may share" and lists "pangalan, email address, at badge na natanggap"; the titles read "Pagsusulit | Mga Batayan ng Quantum Information" and "Survey Pagkatapos ng Kurso".

In the two rewritten tables (entries 39 and 68), every state, syndrome bit string and correction operator is identical to the English, so nothing would mislead a learner. The problem is the column headers, which translate terms that the page's prose keeps in English: "State" becomes "Estado" and "Syndrome" becomes "Sindrom". Everywhere else the page writes "state" (e.g. "standard basis state", "ang state ng nangungunang tatlong qubit"), and entry 38, which defines the term that names this column, writes "*syndrome*", as does entry 46 ("syndrome na $00$"). The headers should be "State | Syndrome | Pagwawasto" to match the prose. "Pagwawasto" already matches the prose, so it can stay.

examples.source: | State | Syndrome | Correction |
examples.translation: | Estado | Sindrom | Pagwawasto |
examples.suggested: | State | Syndrome | Pagwawasto |
examples.why: Entry 38 introduces the term as '*syndrome*' and all the prose uses 'state'. The Hispanized 'Estado'/'Sindrom' in the header don't match the terms the learner was just taught for these columns.

examples.source: | State | Syndrome | Correction |
examples.translation: | Estado | Sindrom | Pagwawasto |
examples.suggested: | State | Syndrome | Pagwawasto |
examples.why: Same mismatch in the phase-flip table: entry 67 introduces it as the counterpart of the first table, and the surrounding prose keeps 'state'/'syndrome' in English.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning, and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 25 keeps the caveat ("slightly different... because we're not working with a query gate, but the idea is similar"), but "kumpara noong sa Deutsch's algorithm" is clunky: "noong sa" is an awkward construction, and the English possessive "Deutsch's" sits inside a Tagalog sentence where a native writer would say "algorithm ni Deutsch". Entry 25 also uses "phenomenon" while entries 37 and 41 use "penomenon", a small spelling inconsistency. The title-case heading in entry 88 ("Quantum Fourier Transform") is fine for a heading and needs no change.

examples.source: It is slightly different this time than it was for Deutsch's algorithm and the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm
examples.translation: Bahagyang naiiba ito sa pagkakataong ito kumpara noong sa Deutsch's algorithm at sa Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm
examples.suggested: Bahagyang naiiba ito ngayon kumpara sa nakita natin sa algorithm ni Deutsch at sa Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm
examples.why: 'kumpara noong sa' is a stiff calque of 'than it was for', and the English possessive 'Deutsch's' is unnatural inside Tagalog. The meaning is intact.

editor_note: Entry 7 keeps the English meaning: output 0 for constant and 1 for balanced, with nothing swapped or dropped. The problem is the figure title "Suliranin ni Deutsch". Entry 3 says the page will use the name *Deutsch's problem*, and entries 6, 8 and 10 all keep "Deutsch's problem" in English. The title should match that name. "Suliranin" is also more literary than the page's usual "problema/problemang".

examples.source: <Figure title="Deutsch's problem">
examples.translation: <Figure title="Suliranin ni Deutsch">
examples.suggested: <Figure title="Deutsch's problem">
examples.why: Entry 3 says the page will use the name *Deutsch's problem*, and every other entry keeps it in English. The figure title uses a different, more literary Tagalog term, so the name is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: The rewritten heading [14] "Iginawad na Badge" renders "Awarded Badge" faithfully and keeps "Badge" in English, the same way entries [12] and [17] do.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and entry 15 ("Sagot" / "Apat.") is correct. Entry 24's heading "Paralel na Programming" uses a different spelling and capitalization from the rest of the page. The body text right below it (entries 23, 25 and 53) says "parallel programming", and the other headings use sentence case ("Mga modelo ng programming", "Mga task workflow"). Entry 5's video title repeats "sinusuri" for both "reviews" and "examines", which reads stiffly.

examples.source: Parallel programming {#parallel-programming}
examples.translation: Paralel na Programming {#parallel-programming}
examples.suggested: Parallel programming {#parallel-programming}
examples.why: The heading is the only place that uses the respelled 'Paralel' and the title-case 'Programming'. The paragraph right under it says 'parallel programming', and the other headings use sentence case.

examples.source: Iskandar Sitdikov reviews quantum and classical programming models and examines how we can combine them
examples.translation: sinusuri ni Iskandar Sitdikov ang quantum at classical na mga modelo ng programming at sinusuri kung paano natin maaaring pagsamahin ang mga ito
examples.suggested: tinatalakay ni Iskandar Sitdikov ang quantum at classical na mga modelo ng programming at sinusuri kung paano natin maaaring pagsamahin ang mga ito
examples.why: Using the same verb twice in one sentence is stiff. Using 'tinatalakay' for 'reviews' reads more naturally and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 3 and 35 are accurate, and entry 35 matches the wording of entry 34 exactly. Entry 48's heading "Klasikal kumpara sa Quantum na Probability?" breaks two conventions the rest of the file keeps: it uses "Klasikal" where the page otherwise always writes "classical" (classical computer, classical probabilism), and it leaves "Probability" in English although the section right below it uses "probabilidad". Entry 67's "Nagbibigay siya ng motibasyon sa business value" copies the English "motivates" word for word and reads stiffly. A Tagalog writer would say he explains why quantum computers have business value.

examples.source: Classical vs. quantum probability?
examples.translation: Klasikal kumpara sa Quantum na Probability?
examples.suggested: Classical kumpara sa quantum na probabilidad?
examples.why: The rest of the file writes 'classical', and the section body (entry 49) uses 'probabilidad'. The heading introduces 'Klasikal', keeps English 'Probability', and adds stray title-case capitals.

examples.source: He motivates the business value of quantum computers by showing the computational states that can be simultaneously realized on a quantum computer.
examples.translation: Nagbibigay siya ng motibasyon sa business value ng mga quantum computer sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakita ng mga computational state na maaaring sabay-sabay na maisakatuparan sa isang quantum computer.
examples.suggested: Ipinapaliwanag niya kung bakit may business value ang mga quantum computer sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakita ng mga computational state na maaaring sabay-sabay na umiral sa isang quantum computer.
examples.why: 'Nagbibigay ng motibasyon sa' copies 'motivates' word for word and reads unnaturally. The English means he argues for or justifies the business value, and it is clearer to say that directly.

editor_note: Entry 12 is a faithful, natural rendering of the Credly notice. It keeps every data-sharing detail, including "ibabahagi ... sa Credly", "sa mga subsidiary ng IBM at sa mga third party sa buong mundo" and "Pamamahalaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy", and it holds the "may" hedge as "Maaaring".

Both rewritten entries are faithful: entry 99 keeps the twirling claim intact ("Binabago ng twirling ang ingay para kahit ang mga simpleng noise model ay maging mas tumpak na representasyon...") with a natural "Pag-alis ng mga \"masamang\" qubit" heading, and entry 136 renders the heading as "Survey Pagkatapos ng Kurso".

Rewritten entry 6 is faithful and natural ("sinusuri ni Olivia ang mga pangunahing quantum physics at matematika na kailangan para sa iyong paglalakbay sa quantum computing"), keeps the 'necessary for' sense and the IBMVideo attributes intact, and is consistent with entry 5's casual register.

None of the three rewritten headings would mislead a learner, but two small things are worth fixing. Entries 54 and 69 render "Post-process" as "Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos". That uses English title case, while the other Tagalog headings on the page use sentence case (e.g. "Layunin sa pag-aaral"). It also switches to a noun, so it no longer matches the sibling step headings "I-map", "I-optimize" and "I-execute", and it drifts from "Post-process" in step [34] and "post-processing" in [70]. Entry 29, "Daloy ng trabaho ng Qiskit patterns", is accurate, but the body text right below it ([28], [30]) keeps "workflow", so the heading and the text it introduces use different words for the same thing.

examples.source: Post-process {#post-process}
examples.translation: Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos {#post-process}
examples.suggested: I-post-process {#post-process}
examples.why: The capital P on 'Pagkatapos' is English title case, and the noun form breaks the imperative pattern of the other steps (I-map / I-optimize / I-execute). It also doesn't match 'Post-process' in step list entry [34].

examples.source: Post-process {#post-process-1}
examples.translation: Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos {#post-process-1}
examples.suggested: I-post-process {#post-process-1}
examples.why: Same problem as entry 54. The step heading should follow the same imperative pattern as I-map / I-optimize / I-execute and match the term 'post-processing' used in entry [70].

examples.source: Qiskit patterns workflow {#qiskit-patterns-workflow}
examples.translation: Daloy ng trabaho ng Qiskit patterns {#qiskit-patterns-workflow}
examples.suggested: Ang Qiskit patterns workflow {#qiskit-patterns-workflow}
examples.why: The translation is accurate, but entries [28] and [30] keep 'workflow' (for example, 'Ang Qiskit patterns workflow ay...'). The heading and the text under it should use the same term.

editor_note: Both rewritten headings mean the same as the English and would not mislead a learner. The problem is consistency. They render "optimization problem" as "problema sa optimisasyon", but everywhere else the page keeps the English term: "optimization problem" in entries 11, 40, 52, 65, 67, 72, 74 and 107, and "Optimization" in entries 36 and 39. As a result, the headings are the only places on the page where the term is Tagalized, and "optimisasyon" appears nowhere else. Changing them to "optimization problem" would match the body text that follows each heading (entries 52 and 65).

examples.source: Graph → optimization problem
examples.translation: Graph → problema sa optimisasyon
examples.suggested: Graph → optimization problem
examples.why: The rest of the file keeps 'optimization problem' in English (e.g. entries 40, 52, 65). This heading is the only place it is Tagalized, so the term is inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: Optimization problem → Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Problema sa optimisasyon → Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: Optimization problem → Hamiltonian
examples.why: Same inconsistency. Entry 52 in the same section says 'Isulat muli ang optimization problem bilang isang Hamiltonian', so the heading should use the same term as the text beneath it.

editor_note: Entry 22's "Library ng graph na Rustworkx" faithfully and naturally renders "Rustworkx graph library", keeping the product name and the pip command unchanged.

Entry 26 is faithful. "Qiskit IBM Transpiler na may AI local mode" keeps the product name and the pip command unchanged, and it uses the same "na may" pattern as the neighbouring requirement entry 24.

Entry 64 is faithful: "primitive na EstimatorV2 na may fake backend" running "parehong AQC-optimized na circuit at ang baseline Trotter circuit, sinusukat ang ZZ observable para sa bawat isa" keeps both circuits and the per-circuit ZZ measurement, and its terms match entry 62.

The translation is faithful throughout, and the technical passages read correctly, including the clique/XY-mixer explanation, pendant nodes and fixed-angle QAOA. There are three small slips. In [14], "given pairwise resource conflicts" becomes "kahit may pairwise resource conflicts" ("even though there are conflicts"). That turns a condition into a concession, although the meaning is still recoverable. In [87], "Sangguni sa" is not a valid imperative and should be "Sumangguni sa". In [18], the comma in "iisang, mas mahigpit na constraint" is calqued from the English.

examples.source: the largest collection of tasks that can execute concurrently given pairwise resource conflicts
examples.translation: na maaaring maisagawa nang sabay-sabay kahit may pairwise resource conflicts
examples.suggested: na maaaring maisagawa nang sabay-sabay batay sa mga pairwise resource conflict
examples.why: 'kahit' means 'even though', so a condition becomes a concession. The English means the tasks run concurrently under the constraint of the conflicts, not despite them.

examples.source: Consult the Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer guide
examples.translation: Sangguni sa [Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer guide]
examples.suggested: Sumangguni sa [Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer guide]
examples.why: 'Sangguni' is the root, not an imperative verb. The correct form is 'Sumangguni'.

examples.line_approx: ay maaaring palitan ng iisang, mas mahigpit na constraint
examples.source: can be replaced by a single, tighter constraint
examples.translation: maaaring palitan ng iisang, mas mahigpit na constraint
examples.suggested: maaaring palitan ng iisa at mas mahigpit na constraint
examples.why: The comma between the modifiers is copied from English punctuation and reads unnaturally in Tagalog.

editor_note: Most of the 21 rewritten headings are faithful and natural (e.g. "Hakbang 1: I-map ang mga classical input sa isang quantum na problema", "Natututo ang KQD ng isang filter na humuhubog muli sa distribusyong ito"). Two paired section headings attach the scale to the wrong noun. "Halimbawa ng small-scale na simulator" [51] reads as "example of a small-scale simulator", and "Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware" [188] reads as "example of large hardware", when the English means a small or large example run on a simulator or on hardware. They also treat "scale" differently, keeping "small-scale" in English but translating "large-scale" as "malakihan". Separately, [71] "Ebolusyon sa paglipas ng oras" and [74] "Pinalawak na swap test" translate terms that the body keeps in English ("time evolution", "extended swap test"), which is a small consistency slip.

examples.source: Small-scale simulator example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng small-scale na simulator
examples.suggested: Small-scale na halimbawa gamit ang simulator
examples.why: 'small-scale' modifies the example, not the simulator. The rendering describes a small simulator.

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware
examples.suggested: Large-scale na halimbawa sa hardware
examples.why: 'malakihang hardware' means big hardware, but the English means a large-scale problem run on hardware. It also doesn't match [51], which keeps 'small-scale' in English.

examples.source: Time evolution
examples.translation: Ebolusyon sa paglipas ng oras
examples.suggested: Time evolution
examples.why: The surrounding prose keeps 'time evolution' / 'time-evolution operator' in English, so the heading's paraphrase doesn't match the term the learner sees in the body.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The three approximations, the weak-coupling condition (x ≫ 1), the differential meson-minus-vacuum protocol and the atol trade-off are all rendered faithfully. The problems are naturalness slips. The two example headings attach the scale to the wrong noun: "Halimbawa ng maliitang simulator" reads as "example of a small simulator" and "Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware" as "example of large hardware". "Define" is spelled in an unusual way ("Idepine", "idinidepine"), "kinakarakter" is awkward, and "ebolusyunin sa oras" and "ay ihinihiwalay" read stiff or non-standard.

examples.source: Small-scale simulator example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng maliitang simulator
examples.suggested: Maliit na halimbawa gamit ang simulator
examples.why: 'Small-scale' describes the example, not the simulator. As written, the heading says the simulator is small.

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware
examples.suggested: Malakihang halimbawa sa hardware
examples.why: Same problem: 'large-scale' is attached to the hardware, not to the example.

examples.source: Each lattice site is characterized by three quantum numbers ... The local fermion number is defined
examples.translation: Ang bawat lattice site ay kinakarakter ng tatlong quantum number ... ay idinidepine mula rito
examples.suggested: Inilalarawan ang bawat lattice site ng tatlong quantum number ... ay tinutukoy mula rito
examples.why: 'kinakarakter' and 'idinidepine' are awkward, ad-hoc Taglish coinages. More established verbs (inilalarawan, tinutukoy) read more naturally.

examples.source: place a meson at the center of the lattice and evolve in time ... isolates the coherent hadron signal
examples.translation: maglagay ng meson sa gitna ng lattice at ebolusyunin sa oras ... ay ihinihiwalay ang coherent hadron signal
examples.suggested: ... at hayaang mag-evolve sa paglipas ng oras ... ay inihihiwalay ang coherent hadron signal
examples.why: 'ebolusyunin sa oras' is a calque. 'ihinihiwalay' is a non-standard form of 'inihihiwalay'.

editor_note: Two sentences change the physics a learner would take away. In [107], "the parity cannot be wrong" became "hindi na maaaring maling mali ang parity", which means "cannot be *very* wrong" and so implies parity can still be slightly off inside a single major shell. In [54], "Single-particle energies are not rescaled" became "Hindi kinukumpuni" ("are not repaired"), which loses the caveat that the (A/A_ref)^-0.3 scaling applies only to the two-body matrix elements. Smaller issues: the typo "katha-thang offset" for "spurious offset" in [165]; "two decades of subspace size" rendered literally as "dalawang dekada" in [133], which reads as ten-year spans rather than orders of magnitude; the stiff calque "fermionic isa" in [174]; and "treats a nucleus as" rendered as "Ginagamit ... ang isang nucleus bilang" ("uses") in [21].

examples.source: so once the nucleon numbers are right the parity cannot be wrong
examples.translation: kaya kapag tama na ang nucleon numbers, hindi na maaaring maling mali ang parity
examples.suggested: kaya kapag tama na ang nucleon numbers, hindi na maaaring mali ang parity
examples.why: 'maling mali' means 'very wrong'. This weakens a definite claim (parity is automatic) into 'parity cannot be badly wrong', which suggests it can still be slightly wrong.

examples.source: Single-particle energies are not rescaled.
examples.translation: Hindi kinukumpuni ang single-particle energies.
examples.suggested: Hindi nire-rescale ang single-particle energies.
examples.why: 'kinukumpuni' means 'repaired/fixed', not 'rescaled'. The learner loses the caveat that the mass scaling does not apply to single-particle energies.

examples.source: adds a spurious offset to every diagonal element
examples.translation: nagdaragdag ng katha-thang offset sa bawat diagonal element
examples.suggested: nagdaragdag ng huwad (spurious) na offset sa bawat diagonal element
examples.why: 'katha-thang' is a malformed word (typo) and it obscures the meaning 'spurious'.

examples.source: traces the bound's descent across two decades of subspace size
examples.translation: sumusundan sa pagbaba ng bound sa dalawang dekada ng laki ng subspace
examples.suggested: sa dalawang order of magnitude ng laki ng subspace
examples.why: 'dekada' is read as ten-year periods. The English means a factor of 100 in subspace size.

examples.source: differs from the fermionic one in the signs of its amplitudes
examples.translation: naiiba ang state na inihahanda nito sa fermionic isa sa *signs*
examples.suggested: naiiba ito sa fermionic na state sa *signs* ng mga amplitude nito
examples.why: 'fermionic isa' is a word-for-word calque of 'the fermionic one' and is not idiomatic Tagalog.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (30, 60, 90, 134, 135) keep the English meaning. Entry 135 keeps the ranking, the budget-or-accuracy condition and the three outputs (local_scales, sampling_costs, residual_bias_bound), and entry 90 correctly says the X measurement on qubit 6 commutes with the X error. Entry 135 has an awkward hybrid verb, "aktibong mi-mitigate-han / hindi mi-mitigate-han". A native editor would use the standard Taglish future form "ima-mitigate". Entry 30 renders "circuit of interest" as "target na circuit", but the Step 3c heading (entry 139) keeps "circuit of interest" in English, so the same concept is named two ways.

examples.source: which errors will be actively mitigated and which will be left unmitigated
examples.translation: kung aling mga error ang aktibong mi-mitigate-han at kung alin ang mananatiling hindi mi-mitigate-han
examples.suggested: kung aling mga error ang aktibong ima-mitigate at kung alin ang hindi ima-mitigate
examples.why: 'mi-mitigate-han' is a malformed affixation that a Tagalog technical writer would not produce; the usual Taglish future form is 'ima-mitigate'.

examples.source: Execute the circuit of interest with anti-noise
examples.translation: Isagawa ang target na circuit gamit ang anti-noise
examples.suggested: Isagawa ang circuit of interest gamit ang anti-noise (or change entry 139 to 'target na circuit')
examples.why: Entry 139 ('Isagawa ang circuit of interest gamit ang antinoise') keeps the English term, so the same concept is named two ways on the page. It does not mislead, but it is inconsistent.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries are faithful; the Open Plan caveat in [27] keeps its full meaning ("hindi mo mapapatakbo ang tutorial na ito gaya ng nakasulat", "dadaan sa buong queue latency"), and [20] keeps "cost Hamiltonian na ang ground state ay nag-e-encode ng optimal na solusyon".

In entry 43, "Probability distribution" became "Pamamahagi ng posibilidad". "Posibilidad" means possibility, not probability. The rest of the page keeps "probability" (entries 40 and 45), so this should say "probability distribution" or "distribusyon ng probabilidad". The rewritten step labels are also inconsistent with the body text. Entry 38 says "Abstraktong Circuit" but entries 27 and 34 say "Abstract circuit". Entry 39 says "Pamamahagi ng quasi-probability" but the next paragraph (entry 40) says "quasi-probability distribution". The heading in entry 46, "Halimbawa ng hardware", reads as "an example of hardware" and doesn't match "hardware example" in entries 24 and 36. None of these would mislead a learner in context, and the remaining rewritten headings (1, 5, 25, 33, 37, 42, 51) are faithful.

examples.source: Input: Probability distribution.
examples.translation: Input: Pamamahagi ng posibilidad.
examples.suggested: Input: Probability distribution.
examples.why: 'Posibilidad' means possibility, not probability. Entries 40 and 45 keep 'probability', and the previous step outputs a quasi-probability distribution, so this label should say the same thing.

examples.source: Input: Abstract circuit.
examples.translation: Input: Abstraktong Circuit.
examples.suggested: Input: Abstract circuit.
examples.why: Entries 27 and 34 render this same step input/output as 'Abstract circuit'. Here it is 'Abstraktong Circuit', so the pipeline labels are inconsistent.

examples.source: Output: Quasi-probability distribution.
examples.translation: Output: Pamamahagi ng quasi-probability.
examples.suggested: Output: Quasi-probability distribution.
examples.why: The very next paragraph (entry 40) says 'quasi-probability distribution'. Using 'pamamahagi' in the label splits the term for no reason.

examples.source: Hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng hardware
examples.suggested: Hardware example
examples.why: The body refers to this section as 'seksyon ng hardware example' (entries 24 and 36). 'Halimbawa ng hardware' reads as 'an example of hardware' rather than 'an example run on hardware'.

editor_note: Entry 13's "Aklatan ng graph na Rustworkx" says the same thing as "Rustworkx graph library". "Aklatan" is a standard Tagalog word for library, and the pip command is left unchanged.

The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The QRMI lifecycle table, the Slurm/SPANK injection passages and the SQD accuracy caveat (23.7 kcal/mol above the reference, no chemical accuracy) are all translated faithfully. A native editor would still fix three small things. Entry [61] copies the English structure word for word, so "kabiguan" (failures) is the thing that releases the session. Entry [76] renders "adjusted circuit" as "naayos", which can read as "repaired". Entry [4] uses the stiff "mababa sa isang minuto" where "wala pang isang minuto" is the natural way to say "under one minute".

examples.source: so that failures after acquisition still release a notebook-owned session
examples.translation: upang ang mga kabiguan pagkatapos ng acquisition ay mag-release pa rin ng session na pag-aari ng notebook
examples.suggested: upang kahit may pumalya pagkatapos ng acquisition, mare-release pa rin ang session na pag-aari ng notebook
examples.why: This copies the English structure word for word, so the failures themselves become the ones that release the session, which sounds robotic in Tagalog.

examples.source: The reported results use this adjusted circuit.
examples.translation: Ginagamit ng iniulat na mga resulta ang naayos na circuit na ito.
examples.suggested: Ang binagong circuit na ito ang ginamit sa mga iniulat na resulta.
examples.why: 'Naayos' leans toward 'fixed/repaired', but the circuit was actually reduced to fit the backend. 'Binago' matches 'adjusted' more closely, and the reordered sentence reads more naturally.

examples.source: under one minute on IBM Quantum hardware
examples.translation: mababa sa isang minuto sa IBM Quantum® hardware
examples.suggested: wala pang isang minuto sa IBM Quantum® hardware
examples.why: For durations, 'wala pang isang minuto' is the idiomatic way to say 'under one minute'. 'Mababa sa' is a literal calque.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. I found no inverted conditions or swapped numbers: the 3+2 and 6+4 compression plans, 0.82 vs 0.98 fidelity, the four hours of classical compression vs 18 QPU minutes, and the note that a caller's estimator_options replaces the defaults instead of merging all come through correctly. There are some wording slips a native editor would fix. In [49], 'coarsely resolved' became 'marahang lang na-resolve' ('gently/slowly resolved', with a typo) when it should be 'magaspang', and 'identical' became 'magkatulad' ('similar'). The verb form 'ni-i-compress' is malformed in [46]. 'Nasa ibabaw pa ng pareho' in [61] is a literal copy of the English 'on top of both', and the admonition title in [60] is half English.

examples.source: On this small exact run the two-spinon continuum is only coarsely resolved, but the machinery is identical to the hardware run that follows.
examples.translation: ang two-spinon continuum ay marahang lang na-resolve, ngunit magkatulad ang mekanismo sa hardware run na susunod.
examples.suggested: ang two-spinon continuum ay magaspang pa lang ang pagka-resolve, pero pareho mismo ang proseso sa hardware run na susunod.
examples.why: 'Marahan' means gently or slowly, not coarse or low-resolution, so the caveat about limited resolution gets blurred. 'Magkatulad' also weakens 'identical' to 'similar'.

examples.source: Each segment ... compresses `k` consecutive Trotter steps ... so here we compress the first three steps
examples.translation: Bawat segment na ... ay ni-i-compress ang `k` na magkakasunod na Trotter steps ... kaya dito, ni-i-compress natin ang unang tatlong steps
examples.suggested: Kino-compress ng bawat segment ang `k` na magkakasunod na Trotter step ... kaya dito, kino-compress natin ang unang tatlong step
examples.why: 'ni-i-compress' is not a valid verb form. It should be actor-focus 'nagko-compress' or object-focus 'kino-compress'.

examples.source: Queue wait is on top of both.
examples.translation: Nasa ibabaw pa ng pareho ang paghihintay sa queue.
examples.suggested: Dagdag pa rito ang paghihintay sa queue.
examples.why: This copies the English idiom 'on top of' word for word; 'nasa ibabaw' means physically above.

examples.source: Reconnecting to a long-running job
examples.translation: Reconnecting sa isang mahabang job na tumatakbo
examples.suggested: Pag-reconnect sa isang matagal na tumatakbong job
examples.why: The title mixes an English gerund with Tagalog. 'Mahabang job na tumatakbo' is also awkward word order for 'long-running'.
